newsitem.title: USA: FDA approves Roche's oral Cytovene.
newsitem.headline: FDA approves Roche's oral Cytovene.

text.p: Hoffman-La Roche, a U.S. based unit of Switzerland's Roche Holding Ltd, said on Tuesday that it has received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval to market oral canciclovir, or Cytovene, for prevention of cytomegalovirus in organ transplant patients.
The approval is based upon data that showed that Cytoven has reduced overall incidence of the life-threatening virus in liver transplant recipients by 78 percent, Hoffman-La Roche said.
Cytomegalovirus disease occurs in 15 percent to 30 percent of all solid organ transplant recipients, primarily in the first three months after a transplant when immunosuppression is most intense.
Previously, the intraveneous form of Cytovene was the only medication indicated to prevent cytomegalovirus in solid organ transplant recipients, Hoffman-La Roche said.
Cytomegalovirus, which is related to the herpes family of viruses, infects 50 percent of the U.S. adult population, the company said.
The virus is in a dormant state in individuals with healthy immune systems, but it erupts in people with compromised immune systems, such as people with AIDS or those receiving organ transplants.
